architectReview.evidence: Leader review of the gate command (G002). Reuses run_collect (no forked run logic), emits a valid JUnit XML (XML-escaped) + JSON summary under testsprite_tests/, and the gh integration is strictly best-effort: it probes gh presence + PR context and only posts on a real PR, otherwise prints a skip note and continues — the gate exit code depends ONLY on test results (0 all-pass else 1), never on gh. Small, cohesive, idiomatic; +3 unit tests (junit escaping/shape). Works with or without an OpenAI key (analysis is additive).

executorQa.evidence: Live e2e (artifacts/gate-e2e.txt): a scratch project with 1 passing + 1 failing backend test against a local server. `testsprite-rs gate` printed 'gate: 1/2 passed (1 failed)', wrote a VALID junit.xml (testsuite tests=2 failures=1, a <failure> element for the failing case) and gate-summary.json (failed/passed/results incl. LLM root-cause), gracefully skipped gh ('not on a PR ... skipping'), and exited 1 — so CI would gate on the failure. build clean, clippy 0, cargo test 16/16 (+3 gate tests).
